\section[das Telefon]{das Telefon — a telephone}

\label{lesson:GE-C82-telefon}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for a bag; a pocket, then the German for money.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: das Telefon}
\textbf{das Telefon} — \textquotedblleft{}a telephone\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{Telefon} $\leftarrow$ French \emph{téléphone}, a modern coinage from Greek \emph{tēle}, \textquotedblleft{}far\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{phōnē}, \textquotedblleft{}sound\textquotedblright{} — borrowed; EtymDB 2.1 traces English \emph{telephone} the same way.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{das Telefon}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{das Telefon}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for a bag; a pocket, then the German for money, then say \emph{das Telefon} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does das Telefon mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A telephone\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: der Baum}

\end{cousinweb}
